table_title: List the major Western philosophers from antiquity through the mid-20th century, with the primary canonical work most closely associated with each, the year of composition or publication, and the philosophical tradition they represent.
db_analog: SELECT philosopher, primary_work, year, tradition FROM major_western_philosophers WHERE era_overlaps('antiquity', 'mid-20th-century') ORDER BY philosopher
temporal_note: 32 Wikipedia URLs (16 per-philosopher articles + 16 per-work articles), accessed 2026-05-12 (Year cells re-verified against per-work articles in cycle-1 repair). Universe is a curator-bounded set of 16 major Western philosophers spanning antiquity (Plato c. 375 BC) through the mid-20th century (Sartre 1943), each paired with their most-canonical primary work. The 16 philosophers are: Plato, Aristotle (Classical Greek); Marcus Aurelius (Hellenistic-Roman); Augustine, Aquinas (Medieval); Machiavelli, Descartes, Locke, Hume (Early Modern); Kant, Hegel, Marx, Nietzsche (Modern); Wittgenstein, Heidegger, Sartre (Contemporary, 20th c.). The 'Primary Work' cell is a curator-selected single work from the set of major works listed in the philosopher's Wikipedia article (lead paragraph + 'Notable works' section); the selection criterion is 'most-anthologized in undergraduate-philosophy reference contexts', which is curator judgment rather than a Wikipedia-source-defined designation. The 'Year' cell is the per-work Wikipedia article's stated completion or publication year, applying the latest-year-in-range convention for works with composition windows: Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics 'no consensus' window 335-322 BCE → staged Year -322 (Aristotle's death year, conventional 'completed-by' date per the per-work article); Marcus Aurelius's Meditations 170-180 AD window → staged Year 180 (Marcus Aurelius's death year, conventional 'completed-by' date per the per-philosopher article); Augustine's City of God 413-426 AD → staged 426 (completion); Aquinas's Summa Theologica 1265-1274 → staged 1274 (Aquinas's death year, unfinished at his death, conventional 'completed-by' date); Plato's Republic c. 375 BC → staged -375 (representative midpoint, well-cited convention). For modern works (post-1500) the staged Year is the verbatim first-edition publication year per the per-work Wikipedia article. Per-row cells: Philosopher name is the conventional English short-form (e.g., 'Aquinas' not 'Thomas Aquinas'; 'Marcus Aurelius' full); Primary Work is the standard English title; Year is the integer year (negative integers for BC dates); Tradition is a 6-value categorical (Classical Greek, Hellenistic-Roman, Medieval, Early Modern, Modern, Contemporary). The universe-bounding ('major Western philosophers, antiquity to mid-20th c.') is curator-defined rather than from a single Wikipedia master list. The 16-row selection reflects philosophers commonly listed as foundational across multiple canonical philosophy reference works (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy, etc.). Underlying biographical and text-attribution facts are stable on a multi-century horizon.
_extraction_notes: Original instance filling the `qualitative` category gap (gap 4 → gap 3 after this staging — one of 3 gap-4 categories remaining before this pick). User-selected qualitative/philosophy from the gap-4 candidate slate. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 32 — one per-philosopher Wikipedia article + one per-work Wikipedia article per row (16 + 16; per-work URLs added in cycle 1 so the Year cell is fully grounded by the cited per-work article). No master list source is used because no single Wikipedia article enumerates 'the major Western philosophers' as a clean source-defined list (`List of philosophers (alphabetical)` is far too broad with thousands of entries; `List of philosophical movements` is prose-only; `Western philosophy` master article is structured as historical-era prose without a single canonical philosopher-list wikitable). The universe is therefore curator-bounded rather than source-defined; this is acknowledged in claim_type and decision_log. Pipeline: (1) curator selected 16 philosophers from a curator-bounded 'major Western philosophers, antiquity to mid-20th c.' set (criteria: each philosopher is universally listed as foundational across major philosophy reference works — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Routledge Encyclopedia of Philosophy, etc.; each has a dedicated Wikipedia article; each has a clear single-most-cited primary work), (2) per-philosopher Wikipedia article fetched for each, (3) Primary Work cell selected by the curator from the set of major works listed in each philosopher's Wikipedia article lead paragraph and 'Notable works' / 'Major works' section — the source LISTS multiple major works; the curator SELECTS one per the 'most-anthologized in undergraduate-philosophy reference contexts' criterion (curator judgment, not Wikipedia-source-defined), (4) Year of composition or publication taken primarily from the per-work Wikipedia article using the 'completed-by / latest year in range / publication year' convention; BC dates rendered as negative integers (Plato's Republic c. 375 BC = -375; Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics completed c. 322 BC = -322 per Nicomachean Ethics article's 335-322 BCE composition window; Marcus Aurelius's Meditations completed c. 180 AD = 180 per Wikipedia's 170-180 AD window with the death-year convention), (5) Tradition assigned to the 6-value categorical based on the philosopher's historical period (Classical Greek for Plato/Aristotle; Hellenistic-Roman for Marcus Aurelius; Medieval for Augustine/Aquinas; Early Modern for Machiavelli through Hume; Modern for Kant through Nietzsche; Contemporary for 20th-c. Wittgenstein/Heidegger/Sartre), (6) sort alphabetically by Philosopher. Result: 16 rows × 4 columns, PK on Philosopher, 0 duplicates. Year range: -375 (Plato's Republic) to 1943 (Sartre's Being and Nothingness). Tradition distribution: Classical Greek 2, Hellenistic-Roman 1, Medieval 2, Early Modern 4, Modern 4, Contemporary 3. Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include the canonical author-work pairings (Plato/Republic, Aristotle/Nicomachean Ethics, Kant/Critique of Pure Reason, Marx/Das Kapital, Nietzsche/Thus Spoke Zarathustra, Wittgenstein/Tractatus, Sartre/Being and Nothingness); mid-difficulty cells include the year of publication for older works (LLMs typically know within 50 years for medieval, within a decade for early modern, within a year for modern); harder calibration cells include the Tradition classification (the 'Hellenistic-Roman' vs 'Medieval' boundary for Marcus Aurelius 180 AD; the 'Modern' vs 'Contemporary' boundary for Nietzsche 1885 vs Wittgenstein 1921) and the Year cells for non-publication-dated works (Plato's Republic dating, Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics dating, Aquinas's Summa Theologica completion year 1274).
